verdict.rationale: Polar's docs describe a fast integration path: "6 lines of code" positioning, official TypeScript and Python SDKs, framework adapters for checkouts and webhooks, no-code checkout links, an isolated sandbox with test cards, and a `polar listen` CLI for testing webhooks locally. That supports a quick, docs-driven payment integration. However, the pack shows no actual copy-paste code snippets per language, documents SDKs only for TypeScript and Python, and has no hands-on evidence of a working flow being built in under a day. missing for 10: verbatim copy-paste code examples across languages, SDK coverage beyond TypeScript/Python, independent or hands-on corroboration of under-a-day integration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can integrate a working payment flow from the docs alone in under a day, with copy-paste examples in my language

citations.quote: Payments & Billing with 6 lines of code.
Our TypeScript & Python SDKs come with a built-in helper function to easily validate and parse the webhook event
Framework adapters make it dead simple to add Polar checkouts and webhooks to your stack.
The sandbox environment allows you to experience the complete customer funnel, including checkout. You can perform test payments using Stripe's test card numbers.
The official Python SDK provides fully typed synchronous and asynchronous clients for the Polar API.
